android.desc:
Take your team's passwords with you wherever you go by downloading Passbolt's open-source mobile app. It offers all the beloved features of the web application, including industry-leading password sharing security, form autofill, plus biometric and multi-factor authentication.

Why choose Passbolt mobile?
- Setting the highest standards in password collaboration security.
- Biometric authentication allows you to log in and access your passwords using fingerprint or facial recognition.
- Secure MFA login is enhanced with NFC-enabled Yubikey support.
- The autofill feature simplifies credential input on your mobile device.
- Fully Open Source.

Passbolt is based in Luxembourg and complies with the EU's strict data privacy regulations. The app's security model follows strict end-to-end encryption principles. A key aspect of this is the secure transfer of private keys from the browser to the app, achieved offline through the scanning of multiple QR codes.

Accessibility Features: Passbolt utilizes these features provided by Android to assist you in signing into both web and native applications using the credentials stored in it.

Discover more at passbolt.com.

quotes.text:
I admit Bitwarden is probably the most advanced, but the alternatives I named above (Psono, Passbolt, Passwork) seem not that far behind and some of your research seems a bit superficial.

> Bitwarden has an Android app (two of those didn't)

That's just wrong. All three of the alternatives I mentioned have an Android app. I haven't used any of them, though.

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.psono.psono

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.passwork.passwork_sh

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.passbolt.mobile.android

> has been security audited (I didn't see anything for those other ones)

A quick search turns up at least some auditing activity:

Passbolt: https://www.passbolt.com/incidents

Psono: https://doc.psono.com/admin/asvs/overview.html (self-audit)

Looking more closely at Passwork, they claim to have open/auditable source code, but I can't find any public code. So they are out of the game anyway.

> Bitwarden has a much better pricing structure around non business users. It has a free tier and plans for families/non business users, as well as business use. Those others had nothing comparable that I could see except for a limited free tier.

Psono's full-featured enterprise version is free for anyone with up to 10 users. I don't see any such generous offer at Bitwarden or elsewhere.

And both, Psono and Passbolt offer unlimited business tiers for only 3€ per user per month which seems to be in the range of what …
